points.description: States that a stack is a data structure that stores elements (a collection of items).
States the LIFO property precisely: the last item added (pushed) is the first item removed (popped), using the term last-in-first-out (LIFO) or equivalent exact wording.
points.partial_credit: Half: describes removal order only roughly (e.g., 'last in comes out first' without naming LIFO or stating removal) but is clearly correct.

points.description: Correctly distinguishes a stack from a queue: a stack removes the most recently added item (LIFO), unlike a queue, which removes the earliest added item (FIFO); no wrong claim about order.
points.partial_credit: Half: implies the contrast correctly (e.g., mentions removal only from the top/most recent end) without explicitly naming the queue/FIFO contrast.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a data structure storing elements plus an exact statement of last-in-first-out removal order, with the LIFO idea clearly distinguished from a queue's FIFO. Vague descriptions (e.g., 'a pile of things', 'stores data') or any wrong order (FIFO) earn nothing for that point. Part marks only where clearly more than half of a point is precisely stated.
